target.scope: Vintage (pre-~2005, ideally 80s/90s) tees and crewnecks from tool/trade brands: Milwaukee Electric Tools, Klein Tools, DeWalt, Craftsman, Bosch, Makita, Hitachi, Hilti, Ryobi, Metabo, Husky, Matco, CAT, Stihl, Husqvarna, Black & Decker, Porter-Cable, Ingersoll-Rand, John Deere. OUT OF SCOPE (Drew, 2026-10-06): Snap-on, Mac Tools, and racing shirts of any brand (NASCAR/NHRA/motocross, driver or race-team graphics, incl. DeWalt Sadler/Kenseth) = PASS-SCOPE.
target.size: Men's L or XL only. 90s cuts run a size big — judge by pit-to-pit 22-24 in when stated; ask for measurements when not.
target.era: Made before 2016 (Drew, 2026-10-05); 80s/90s preferred. Classic band = pre-2000, judged by single stitch, period blanks and Made in USA. Late band = 2000-2015, eligible ONLY with dating evidence (printed copyright year, dated event/race, driver/sponsor years, retired logo/platform such as Hitachi pre-HiKOKI or Milwaukee V28). Undatable 2000s-or-later = PASS (Klein: WATCH).
hot: Any confirmed-vintage Klein Tools shirt/sweatshirt L/XL up to ~$75 (unicorn: ~3 vintage Klein tees exist on market, none L/XL)
Milwaukee Electric Tools 80s/90s tee <=$60 or crew <=$90, L/XL
Any single-stitch/pre-2000 tool-brand tee <=$30 or crew <=$50, L/XL
Late band (2000-2015, dated): Klein shirt/sweatshirt L/XL up to ~$75; other brands' graphic-led tee <=$20 or crew <=$35, L/XL, good condition
Named grails <=~$60: DeWalt Cordless Not Gutless / DeWalt Challenge promos, Hitachi Mean Green Building Machine, Craftsman There Are Guarantees in Life crew
target.autoPass: Print-on-demand (Gildan/Bella+Canvas/Next Level, 'S + more' menus, Located in Indonesia); brand retro reissues (Klein Est.1857/150th, Snap-on Faded USA Made/Retro Racing, Milwaukee 1924 heritage); listings hiding the tag; parody prints. DeWalt era: Sadler/Dotter=mid-90s, Kenseth #17 Chevy=1998-99, Kenseth #17 Ford=2000-12 (late band, not 90s despite titles), Kenseth #20=2013-15 late band only if dated. 2016+ markers: Milwaukee 1924/100th, Packout, ONE-KEY; Snap-on 100th; Metabo HPT/HiKOKI; DeWalt FlexVolt/Atomic; Ryobi ONE+ HP; Gildan Softstyle tear-away tags. Kurt Busch was never DeWalt.
target.priceGuide: Niche tiers (asks, no sold comps yet): $5-40 common / $40-100 good / $130-700 grail. OBO listings likely close 10-25% under ask.
target.taste: No flag-waving 'Made in America' graphics (giant AMERICAN/USA type, flag+eagle, 'Pride of America', patriotic flag prints): auto PASS-TASTE. Drew reads 90s anti-outsourcing patriotism as jingoistic now. A small 'Made in USA' line inside a brand graphic (e.g. 90s Milwaukee) is on the edge but OK; a plain eagle without the flag is OK.

channels.notes: eBay/Etsy/Grailed/Depop/Mercari 403 plain WebFetch — use browser pane; Mercari and Facebook need real Chrome. Depop prices include buyer fees. Grailed is a markup market: find the piece there, buy it on eBay/Mercari. Gem (gem.app) aggregates everything incl. indie shops. Facebook Marketplace not yet swept for this hunt. 2026-10-04: eBay search pages sometimes return 'Error Page' on navigate; in-page fetch('/sch/...') and fetch('/itm/...') from an ebay.com tab work and parse fine. Etsy/Depop/Poshmark also work via same-origin fetch after loading the homepage. 2026-10-05 Makita probe: US eBay 'makita' clothing is mostly POD spam ('Made in USA/AUS S-2XL') + 2000s Team Makita Suzuki MX. Japanese supply lives on jp.mercari.com and auctions.yahoo.co.jp (both render in the in-app browser; search 'makita 企業', 'マキタ 古着', 'マキタ Tシャツ'). Japanese tags run a size small — judge only by 身幅 (body width) in cm: 56-61cm = 22-24in. Buying needs a proxy (Buyee/ZenMarket), roughly +$25-40 landed.
